newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PORTO FACE CLEAR RUN TO TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PORTO FACE CLEAR RUN TO TITLE.

text.p: Taciturn Porto coach Antonio Oliveira may deny it, but few doubt that his club have sown up the title for what would be Porto's first hat-trick of championship successes.

"Champions" was the single word headline chosen by two of Portugal's three national sports dailies on the day after Porto came to Lisbon's Stadium of Light and beat Benfica, their only serious rivals, 2-1 on Saturday.
The win opened up a cavernous lead of eight points for Porto at the top of the table, with second-placed Benfica in turn three points ahead of city foes Sporting in third.

There are still 19 of the season's 34 league matches to play and in other countries -- ask England's Newcastle who last year squandered a 12-point lead to lose the championship -- such a point advantage might not seem unsurmountable.

But Porto and Benfica have between them won 18 of the last 20 Portuguese league titles -- with Sporting taking the other two -- and the outcome of the championship tends to depend on their head-to-head clashes.

Porto, unbeaten so far in domestic or European competition this season, have now defeated both their traditional rivals on their home grounds in Lisbon and can have little to fear from the return matches.
Sporting were dispatched 1-0 earlier in the season.

In a match between Portugal's two former European Cup winners Porto were simply too good for Benfica on Saturday and sent out a clear warning to England's Manchester United who they face in the quarter finals of Europe's top club championship in a couple of months.
Clinical finishing, tight defence and an inventive midfield in which Brazil's Edmilson Pimenta and Slovenian Zlatko Zahovic outstanding, were the keys to victory.
Once again Brazil's Jardel, the league's top-scorer with 13 goals at nearly one a game in his first season in Portugal, did the damage.

Living up to his 'killer' nickname, he punished the Benfica defence in the 23rd minute when Jorge Soares gave him just too much room inside the area. Jardel controlled a cross from Pimenta on the right and rifled the ball on the volley past Michel Preud'Homme in the Benfica goal.

Benfica captain Joao Vieira Pinto put Benfica back in the hunt with an equaliser at the beginning of the second half, but his Porto counterpart Jorge Costa restored order when he bundled the ball into the net after Preud'Homme had failed to gather a fiercely-struck free-kick.

"You cannot really say that Benfica played badly. It was just that Porto is probably just too much for the state of soccer in Portugal today," wrote sports daily Bola. If Porto do win the title they will join Benfica and Sporting in winning a hat-trick of championships.
Benfica have performed the feat five times while Sporting have performed it twice and are the only club to win the title four seasons running, which they did from 1951-54.
The way things are going, there would be few betting against Porto matching that achievement in the spring of 1998.
